title: Playing drums softly and a woman who refused a drummer
summary: He tells of a woman who hated drums until she heard how softly he played, and describes his light touch and steady time, including filling in for another drummer at the Moulin Rouge.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You think because of the snares or why do they call it a string? Not because it was a bass, I mean a bass drum in it or a drum, that it couldn't play soft. Yeah. You could use a drum just like you, and use it that you could hear all about the instrument. I go as to sign up a job on Audubon Street one day. And lady called me up. I goes up there to see her. And I mentioned to her about how many pieces I had in the band. And I began to call them out. When I say drums, she liked to jump out of her clothes. I said, oh, no indeed. I said, what's the matter, lady? She said, well, I wouldn't have that up in here. I said, well, I'm the drummer. And you called me. And I said, you wouldn't want to give all them fellas a job and shet myself out of that. Oh, no, she said, but I wouldn't want no drums. I said, now, lady, I tell you what I'm going to do. You hire the band. Just hire the band. And if you don't like the drum, when we come up here at night, stop the band. Just keep the rest of the instrument you want to keep, and everything will come out all right. I ain't going to force you to take the drum. But I'm the manager of my band, and I'm the drummer. And I'm not going to shit myself out of a piece of bread to help the other guy. So I said, if you don't like it that night, I won't play. You know what that lady told her that night? When I was playing a band, she come to me, she said, Mr., I ain't never know the drum could play that soft. Well, I mean, she heard all the other instruments. And I never used no jazz sticks, no. Use the regular sticks. Regular sticks. Regular sticks. But I forgot to say it myself, I'm very light on drums. And I ain't never had no complaints since I've been playing with a different band. As Nene Strapania, I went on his job one night at the Moulin Rouge at the West End. Oh yeah. And he was playing with Papa. And I went out there and the fellas said, man, I wish they'd send you at you all the time. Is he a pretty noisy drummer? No, but they claim I'm working better than him. So, all right. But I always would go on the job with an excuse. You know, before I start playing, I would want to find out how they work, you know, so I could work with them like they wanted me. And everybody, I'm not bragging on myself, but everybody I work with, like the time of music up there. See, I keep such good time. I don't try to make no whole lot of explosion like any other fella. I would make some time what I can, what I can't. I leave it alone. If I think I'm a spoiled something, I don't fool with them. And I always keep good time. That's my particular way of doing it.
